title: Watchdogs, debugging, and production patterns

spans.text: LESSON PURPOSE

Goal: apply “Watchdogs, debugging, and production patterns” to a real program or device. The key principle is: A watchdog triggers recovery but does not identify the root cause; retain logs, measurements, and fault records. In a project, follow this guidance: Feed the watchdog only after progress; do not report a permanently blocked task as healthy.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
EXAMPLE CODE
EXPECTED RESULT
Serial Monitor prints alive; watchdog API availability and configuration depend on ESP-IDF/Arduino Core versions.
CORE EXPLANATION

A watchdog restarts a system when expected progress stops; use it as a health contract, not as a blind reset. Tasks should report progress only after useful work, and logs or core dumps should help diagnose blocking and deadlocks. Production firmware also needs bounded queues, timeouts, retry/backoff, stack measurements, and a recovery plan.

are Espressif ESP-IDF APIs exposed by some Arduino-ESP32 core versions, not portable Arduino APIs. For another board, implement an appropriate health/timeout strategy and verify the selected core's support.
IMPORTANT LINE BREAKDOWN
Key line:
#include <esp_task_wdt.h>

What it does: A watchdog triggers recovery but does not identify the root cause; retain logs, measurements, and fault records.
Why it is used: Feed the watchdog only after progress; do not report a permanently blocked task as healthy.
If omitted or changed: ESP-IDF watchdog APIs vary by target/version; verify the Arduino-ESP32 API and board configuration.
